title: A transparent four-spin trial supplies a distinct weaker result
statement: For pairs, singlet-triplet positivity gives <S1.S2>+3/4>=|a|^2+|b|^2+a dot b. At alpha.5 the sharp two-producible floor is-3/8, attained by nearest-neighbor singlet dimers. For0<=alpha<=1, floor>=-3/8-|alpha-.5|/2. The supplied physical four-spin singlet has amplitudes2 on0101/1010 and-1 on other two-up configurations,normalizedsqrt12, NN ring energy-2 and diagonal sum+.5. Its tiled upper=-.5+alpha/8 gives depth>=3 for1/3<alpha<3/5, with sufficient kBT/J1 <(3alpha-1)/(8ln2) below.5 or(3-5alpha)/(8ln2) above.5. This explicit new trial is too weak for depth6. For IID physical preparations at alpha.5, exchange-weighted random bond and random Pauli axis yield Y=(9/4)xi, E Y=e/J1; Hoeffding error<=2exp(-m epsilon^2/10.125). The displayed99% half-.01409 margin uses~1,080,864 samples before physical noise,calibration,drift/cooling. Energy-entanglement gaps, multipartite witnesses and symmetric-replica relaxations are established antecedents. Structured SDP/DMRG/tensor methods remain stronger for other energy/phase estimation tasks; no equal-resource runtime or accuracy win. Phase-sensitive dimer response, novelty and general competing-phase prediction remain open; unrelated N130/N198/N1077/N1274 contracts supply no hidden transfer.

Physical cooling, state preparation and measurement were not performed. IID bond/axis measurement contract needs about1,080,864 independently prepared samples for the displayed99%/half-margin target, before calibration, drift and readout costs.
